transcript: When I left my home to attend Glass. Kill. What If If Only. Imp. at The Public, I unfortunately forgot my umbrella and my thinking cap. This is one of the more experimental pieces I've seen at The Public, and it was frankly a little too out there for my taste. Essentially, it's a set of four one-act plays, each notably different in themes, characters, and even writing styles. There are instances where performers embody abstract concepts, feelings, or inanimate objects, for example. Although each play is distinct, I think the connecting thread between them is how they question the way we internalize and project narratives onto ourselves and the world around us. The production itself was strong, with great performances and design elements, but I'm not sure I was in the right headspace to be able to properly engage with this piece. It’s the kind of show that requires a lot of mental context switching and ultimately brings up more questions than answers. I was most fond of the final play, Imp, which happens to be the most naturalistic of the four and features a really stunning performance by Deirdre O'Connell. But overall, I wish I had been familiar with other work by Caryl Churchill, as I think this could have primed me for the underlying surrealism and ambiguity that runs through this collection of plays. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
